page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. The memory configuration consists of 4.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1.0 GB per core allocation. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance mostly in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests register weak results at 1403.59 and 3699.56 respectively. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read speeds at 27.14 GB/sec and write speeds at 22.64 GB/sec. While bzip3 single-threaded decompression and Geekbench text processing achieve average performance, multi-threaded decompression and Passmark memory scores fall into the poor category. Database operations via Redis SET reach 3.65 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 4.05 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the n2-highcpu-4 offers an entry-level compute-focused profile. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have minimal memory footprints. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs, combined with weak multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks, makes it unsuitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data science, or heavy compilation tasks. It is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, basic text processing, single-threaded decompression utilities, and low-traffic web serving.
